subject: Dedicated capacity provisioning — Apogee final-sizing and provisional hold
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity provisioning — Apogee final-sizing and provisional hold

Team —

Quick ask: Apogee (large POC -> committed production if latency/cost checks out) is pushing to finalize Dedicated sizing this week. They signalled an intent to commit to a 6–12 instance equivalent for a 6-month period, with EU data residency. We need an internal availability read and a short provisional hold so Sales can present a concrete MPO (mutual plan of operations) and get legal to prep a short MOU.

Key ask:
- Can Infra ops confirm how many A100-80GB equivalents we can map to a 6-month dedicated slice starting 2026-07-01 (target go-live)?
- If A100s are tight, provide an H100-equivalent mapping and the delta in expected token-throughput (ballpark).
- Recommend a conservative provisional hold window we can offer (30/45/60 days) given Q3 ramp pressure.

I attached the latest Apogee requirements (apogee_mop_v1.pdf) and an earlier capacity snapshot that might help. I also pasted the high-level concurrency and latency targets below.

Apogee asks:
- sustained concurrent inference workers: ~240 qps (p95 latency target 150ms for generation)
- expected steady token output: ~30M tokens/day first month, ramping to ~90M tokens/day by month 3
- retention: EU-only, optional private deployment later

If we can get a quick inventory + recommended hold, I’ll loop Legal and Sales Ops. Thanks — Jordan

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning — Apogee final-sizing and provisional hold

Jordan —

Thanks for the context. Quick inventory snapshot (courtesy of cluster-ops):
- Free A100-80GB equivalents in EU pools: 4 full units (can be treated as 4x A100-80GB)
- Available H100-80GB type (split across two regions but EU-eligible): 8 units (note: H100 throughput per unit ~1.6x A100 for transformer workloads, but pricing model differs)

Sizing recommendation (ballpark):
- To meet 240 qps with p95 ~150ms, we should aim for the 6 A100-80GB equivalent floor. That gives headroom for autoscaling bursts.
- Operationally, we can offer 6 A100-equivalent dedicated instances OR 4 A100 + 4 H100 mapped as an A100-equivalent pool with a compatibility adapter. The second option likely reduces queuing and improves peak tail latency.

Provisional hold guidance:
- 45 days is reasonable for a holding window given upcoming Q3 commitments; anything longer needs OBO (Operations Board) approval.
- We’ll need a quick capacity activation ticket to reserve node slots and flag scheduling (I can create it once Sales Ops confirms).

I’m attaching the raw capacity snapshot (capacity_snapshot_may20.csv) and will run a more detailed throughput simulation if you want numbers on expected token/sec per configuration.

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity provisioning — Apogee final-sizing and provisional hold

Marissa / Ops —

Forwarding Karthik’s snapshot. Can Sales Ops kick off a provisional hold for APG-48291 for 45 days (target activation window 2026-07-01)? Please create the internal ticket and attach the MOU draft; Legal should be looped for EU residency language. I’ve started a draft MOU (attached draft_mou_apogee.docx) — make any edits you need.

Two asks:
1) Sales Ops: create the hold ticket and flag for node scheduling; set hold expiration 45 days from activation unless deal milestone hit.
2) Legal/Compliance: prepare EU-only data residency clause and a standard SLA exception for p95 latency guarantees given dedicated pool.

FYI I’ll reach out to Apogee for their deployment preferences (H100 vs A100).

—
Jordan

From: Claire Morgan <claire@apogee.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-23T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning — Apogee final-sizing and provisional hold

Jordan / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We’ve reviewed the recommendation internally — Apogee can commit to a 6-instance A100-equivalent Dedicated pool for an initial 6-month period, contingent on:

- EU-only data residency and logging
- A 45-day provisional capacity hold while contracts are finalized
- DocuSign MOU for the provisional commit and a follow-on Dedicated contract (we’ll need to review the MOU language on latency credits)

We prefer an all-A100 mapping if feasible, but would accept the mixed H100/A100 config if it materially improves tail latency. Please send the MOU for signature and the HubSpot link so our procurement team can track.

Claire Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering, Apogee AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Claire Morgan <claire@apogee.ai>, Apogee Legal <legal@apogee.ai>
Date: 2026-05-25T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning — Apogee final-sizing and provisional hold

Thanks all — alignment confirmed. Actions and owners:

- Marissa: open Ops ticket to lock 6 A100-80GB equivalents in EU pool, provisional hold length 45 days (activation planned 2026-07-01). Please attach draft_mou_apogee.docx and capacity_snapshot_may20.csv.
- Karthik: please update the cluster-ops flag and include a short H100 fallback mapping in the ticket.
- Priyom: loop Legal to prepare EU residency clause and the DocuSign MOU link (Claire — you’ll get DocuSign once Legal finalizes).
- Jordan (me): I’ll update the HubSpot deal (HS-48291) and confirm timeline with Apogee procurement.

Attachments: draft_mou_apogee.docx, capacity_snapshot_may20.csv, apogee_mop_v1.pdf

Goal: reserve the capacity so Sales has a deterministic offer to present in the next partner call. If Ops needs additional approvals beyond 45 days I’ll escalate.

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
